# dotnet-inspect

CLI for inspecting .NET libraries and NuGet packages — what `docker inspect` is for containers.

```bash
dotnet-inspect System.Text.Json                    # bare name → routes to best resource
dotnet-inspect type --package System.Text.Json      # discover types
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json  # inspect members
dotnet-inspect diff --package System.Text.Json@9.0.0..10.0.0     # API diff
dotnet-inspect find "Stream*,Diction*"              # search types across scopes
dotnet-inspect extensions HttpClient --reachable   # extension methods (+ reachable types)
dotnet-inspect implements Stream --platform        # implementors across platform
dotnet-inspect depends 'INumber<TSelf>'            # type hierarchy / package deps / library refs
```

Run `dotnet-inspect <command> --help` for flag details. This document teaches the mental model.

## Mental Model

### Library vs Package

These are different resources, not different locations:

- **Library** — a single assembly (.dll). Metadata: version, TFM, compilation flags, type/method counts.
- **Package** — a NuGet bundle (libraries + content). Metadata: license, repository, readme, TFM list.

The same name can refer to either: `library System.Text.Json` vs `package System.Text.Json`.

### Bare Name Router

`dotnet-inspect System.Text.Json` routes to the best resource. Platform libraries are preferred over NuGet packages. The `Source` field confirms which was chosen. Use explicit commands (`library`, `package`) to override.

### Output: Formatters × Verbosity

**Formatters** control rendering: plaintext (default), markdown (`-v` or `--markdown`), oneline (`--oneline`), json (`--json`). Each command picks a sensible default.

**Verbosity** controls which sections are included — `-v:q` (heading only) → `-v:m` (main section) → `-v:n` (all local) → `-v:d` (all, including network-dependent source/IL).

These are orthogonal and compose freely: `-v:n --plaintext` gives all local sections in plaintext. Exception: `--oneline` and `-v` cannot be combined.

### Structured Queries

Like Go templates, without a DSL. Discover the schema, then select and project:

```bash
dotnet-inspect System.Text.Json -D                          # list sections
dotnet-inspect System.Text.Json -D --effective              # sections with data (dry run)
dotnet-inspect library System.Text.Json -D --tree           # full schema tree
dotnet-inspect System.Text.Json -S Symbols --fields "PDB*"  # select section, project fields
dotnet-inspect type System.Text.Json --columns Kind,Type    # project columns in tables
```

### Filtering

- `-k Kind` — filter by kind: `class`/`struct`/`interface`/`enum`/`delegate` (type) or `method`/`property`/`field`/`event`/`constructor` (type single-type view, member)
- `-t Pattern` — glob filter on type names
- `-m Name` — member name filter (supports globs and `Type.Member` dotted syntax)
- `-m N` (numeric) — item limit (members per kind)
- `-n N` or `-N` — line limit (like `head -N`)

Never pipe through `head`/`tail`/`Select-Object` — use `-n` instead.

### Scope Flags (search commands)

`find`, `extensions`, `implements`, `depends` accept scope flags. They're combinable:

- (none) — default curated set
- `--platform` — all platform frameworks (bool flag, not a library name)
- `--extensions` — curated Microsoft.Extensions.* packages
- `--aspnetcore` — curated Microsoft.AspNetCore.* packages
- `--package Name` — specific NuGet package (repeatable)

On `type`/`member`/`library`/`diff`, `--platform` takes a library name (string), not bool.

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| ------- | ------- |
| `type` | Discover types. All-types view (oneline table) or single-type view (tree/shape) |
| `member` | Inspect members. Docs on by default. `--select` for overload indices, `Name:N` to drill in |
| `find` | Search types by glob or fuzzy match across scopes. Comma-separated batch patterns |
| `diff` | Compare API surfaces between versions (`@old..new`). Breaking/additive classification |
| `extensions` | Extension methods/properties for a type. `--reachable` walks the API surface |
| `implements` | Types implementing an interface or extending a base class |
| `depends` | Dependency graphs — type hierarchy, package deps, or library refs (depends on input) |
| `library` | Assembly metadata, symbols, references. `--source-link-audit` for provenance |
| `package` | NuGet metadata, versions, files, layout, dependencies, readme |
| `samples` | Code samples via SourceLink (coverage varies by package) |
| `demo` | Curated showcase queries |
| `cache` | Cache management (`--clean` to clear) |

## Key Gotchas

- **Generic types**: use `'Option<T>'` not `"Option<>"`. The `<>` form resolves to the abstract base, hiding constructors. Quote to prevent shell glob expansion.
- **Inherited members**: derived types only show their own members. Query the base type too.
- **`-v:d` is expensive**: it fetches source/IL. Use default (compact) for scanning, `-v:d` only when you need source code for a specific overload.
- **Diff syntax**: single arg with `..` range — `@8.0.0..9.0.0`, not two separate args.
- **Member requires a type**: `member -m SerializeObject --package Foo` fails. Use `member JsonConvert --package Foo -m SerializeObject` or dotted: `-m JsonConvert.SerializeObject`.
- **Latest version**: `package Foo --version` prints the latest version. `package Foo@8.0.0` or `--version 8.0.0` pins to a specific version. `--versions` lists all available versions.

## Migration Workflow

When code breaks due to API changes:

```bash
dotnet-inspect diff --package System.CommandLine@2.0.0-beta4.22272.1..2.0.3  # what changed?
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine@2.0.3             # new API surface
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine@2.0.3 --select    # overload indices
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine@2.0.3 -m SetAction:1  # drill in
```

Start with `diff` — it shows all removed/changed/added members immediately.
